mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% in a single month reduces near-term discount rates, lowering the present value of expected future dividends and equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% in a single month
regime_hint: Rising short-term interest rate surprise in a steady inflation regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns do not fall below the 5-day average during the same period, or the 5-day return is not statistically significant (p > 0.05) relative to the pre-rate hike period.

mechanism_narrative: When the 12-month change in CPIAUCSL exceeds +0.6%, it indicates accelerating inflation expectations, prompting the market to discount future earnings more aggressively and producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
regime_hint: High-inflation expectations in a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day and 60-day forward returns are both positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) compared to the 12-month pre-inflation spike window.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in monthly PAYEMS (labor market strength) of at least 2% for three consecutive months is associated with stronger corporate hiring intentions and higher expected earnings growth, which drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month for 3 consecutive months
regime_hint: Labor market tightening with rising wage growth
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative or not statistically different from the prior 20-day average during the same labor expansion window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly index of RSAFS (retail sales) falls by more than 5% in two consecutive months, it signals weakening consumer demand, which compresses earnings growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: RSAFS decreases by >5% in two consecutive months
regime_hint: Early signs of a consumer demand recession
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the same demand contraction period.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp decline in INDPRO (industrial production) by at least 8% in a single month, accompanied by a parallel rise in HOUST (housing starts), suggests a supply-side shock that outpaces absorption, pushing down near-term earnings expectations and generating negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls >8% while HOUST rises in the same month
regime_hint: Discrepancy between manufacturing and housing supply in a growth cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (p < 0.05) during the same month, or the correlation between INDPRO and HOUST falls below 0.3.

mechanism_narrative: When UNRATE (unemployment rate) falls below 3.5% for two consecutive months in a low-inflation environment, it signals a tight labor market that raises wage growth expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE < 3.5% for two consecutive months and CPIAUCSL < 280
regime_hint: Labor market tightening in a low-inflation regime
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero (p > 0.05) during the same low-unemployment window.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged period of FEDFUNDS below 1% for four consecutive months creates a risk-on environment by lowering real borrowing costs, which amplifies equity valuation multiples and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns remain negative or flat, and the 20-day forward return is also non-positive during the policy window.

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of GDPC1 (GDP) exceeds the 2023 Q4 level by at least 2% while INDPRO remains flat for two months, it suggests a reacceleration in economic demand that outpaces supply, pushing up earnings expectations and producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 MA(3) > GDPC1_Q4_2023 + 2% and INDPRO is flat for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during the same expansion window, or the correlation between GDPC1 and INDPRO falls below 0.4.
